newsitem.title: USA: Shelby Williams eliminates short-term debt.
newsitem.headline: Shelby Williams eliminates short-term debt.

text.p: Shelby Williams Industries Inc, which makes seating for restaurants, lodging, healthcare and other markets, said Wednesday it had no short-term debt as of June 30, compared with $4.7 million a year ago.
Shelby Williams said continued strong sales and net income enabled it to improve its balance sheet.

Earlier, Shelby Williams reported second quarter earnings of $0.29 a share, up from $0.23 a year ago. Sales were $45.4 million, compared with $41.2 million a year ago excluding sales from a divested division.
The company said its backlog of unshipped orders following a one-week vacation shutdown stood at $35.6 million, compared with $34.9 million a year earlier.

"As has been the case over the last several quarters, hotel refurbishing activity remains brisk," Paul Steinfeld, chairman, said in a statement. "Shelby Williams continues to service a significant portion of that activity as well as business in new hotel construction, restaurants, casinos and other core markets."
